claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr is susceptible to oxygen ingress and oxidation at high temperatures.
Anti-oxidation coatings are required to make this refractory alloy family suitable for high-temperature use in air.
ALD can deposit an ultra-thin, conformal, highly adherent alumina coating on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed alumina coating is tens to a few hundred nanometers thick.
The ALD alumina coating forms a surface barrier that limits oxygen diffusion into HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina layer remains robust and effectively oxygen-impermeable near 1000 °C in air for exposures up to 100 hours under tensile loading.
Oxygen ingress causes oxidation-induced degradation of the microstructure responsible for the alloy's ductility and strength.
The alumina coating will significantly reduce oxidation relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
After the proposed treatment and exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After the proposed treatment and exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C will remain between 163 and 530 MPa.
The proposed operating boundary is approximately 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere for up to 100 hours and tensile strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
Coating performance under cyclic thermal or mechanical loading and over longer exposures is uncertain.
